articles.title: Huang's Ties to Trump Under Scrutiny After Spy Claim
articles.description: Bloomberg's Mike Shepard said that actions taken by the Trump administration and by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang are coming under sharper scrutiny by Congress amid investigations into the affair Huang had with a women alleged to be a Chinese spy. Trump had denied that he knew anything about the national security risks posed by Huang's affair, but recent New York Times reporting reveals that Trump had been briefed about the risk before his trip to China earlier this year. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Nvidia China Scandal Demands Answers, Says Congressman
articles.description: Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi says Congress needs answers from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over his reported relationship with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence, and says lawmakers could consider a subpoena if Huang doesn’t voluntarily appear. The Illinois Democrat also calls for a review of Nvidia’s China export licenses and tougher controls designed to prevent advanced US chips from reaching restricted Chinese entities. He joins Riley Griffin on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Suicides Raise Alarm Inside US Cybersecurity Agencies
articles.description: At least 11 National Security Agency and US Cyber Command workers died by suicide over roughly the past year, according to US officials and public records. Bloomberg’s Jake Bleiberg discusses the intense workload facing personnel at the NSA and Cyber Command amid global conflicts, why the death are raising concerns among senior officials in Congress and the White House, and the efforts to increase mental health support for a workforce critical to US national security. He joins Riley Griffin on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Courts Should Employ a Simpler Fair Use Analysis for Noncompeting Criticism
articles.description: Copyright and trademark rights act in tension with the First Amendment. Indeed, “unlike other property rights, [these] are a form of content-based, government-imposed speech restriction.” (Mark Lemley and Eugene Volokh, Freedom of Speech and Injunctions in Intellectual Property Cases, 48 Duke L.J. 147, 206 (1998)). As such, courts have determined that criticism, generally, puts the critic beyond the reach of a copyright or trademark claim.
